Rule in plain English: An annual rate is turned into a daily one. The divisor depends on the year basis set for the product: 360, 365, or 366 in a leap year.
COBOL as written: IF YEAR-BASE-360  MOVE .0027778 TO WSI-DAY-FACTOR ; IF YEAR-BASE-365  MOVE .0027397 TO WSI-DAY-FACTOR ; IF YEAR-BASE-366  MOVE .0027322 (leap) / .0027397 TO WSI-DAY-FACTOR
Notes: .0027778 = 1/360, .0027397 = 1/365, .0027322 = 1/366. Leap year is tested from OC-TODAYS-JULIAN.

Rule in plain English: Days between the date interest was last accrued through and the new accrue-through date.
COBOL as written: MOVE CM-DTE-ACCR-THRU TO WS-DTE-DATE-2 ; MOVE WS-ACCR-THRU-DTE TO WS-DTE-DATE-1 ; PERFORM ZZZZ-ELAPSED-DAYS -> WS-DTE-RESULT ; MOVE WS-DTE-RESULT TO WSI-DAYS
Notes: Drives every accrual below. CM-DTE-LST-ACCR keeps the previous value for audit.

Rule in plain English: Balance x annual rate x daily fraction. This is the base case when the product has no rate bands.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WSI-ACCRUAL ROUNDED = WSI-AMNT * WSI-RATE-1 * WSI-DAY-FACTOR
Notes: WSI-AMNT is the interest-bearing balance for the bucket being processed (cash or retail).

What it computes: One day's interest — two rate bands
Rule in plain English: The balance up to the first limit is charged at rate 1; everything above it at rate 2.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WSI-ACCRUAL ROUNDED = ; (WSI-LIMIT-1 * WSI-RATE-1 ; + (WSI-AMNT - WSI-LIMIT-1) * WSI-RATE-2) * WSI-DAY-FACTOR
Notes: Tiered pricing. Applied when the balance exceeds WSI-LIMIT-1 but not WSI-LIMIT-2.

What it computes: One day's interest — three rate bands
Rule in plain English: Band 1 up to limit 1 at rate 1, band 2 between the two limits at rate 2, the remainder at rate 3.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WSI-ACCRUAL ROUNDED = ; (WSI-LIMIT-1 * WSI-RATE-1 ; + (WSI-LIMIT-2 - WSI-LIMIT-1) * WSI-RATE-2 ; + (WSI-AMNT - WSI-LIMIT-2) * WSI-RATE-3) * WSI-DAY-FACTOR
Notes: Full three-tier ladder — the most general interest shape in the MY portfolio.

What it computes: One day's interest — flat top rate
Rule in plain English: Whole balance charged at rate 3, used where the product prices everything at the top band.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WSI-ACCRUAL ROUNDED = WSI-AMNT * WSI-RATE-3 * WSI-DAY-FACTOR
Notes: Terminal branch of the banding logic.

What it computes: Scale one day's interest to the period
Rule in plain English: One day's interest multiplied by the number of days since the last accrual.
COBOL as written: MULTIPLY WSI-DAYS BY WSI-ACCRUAL ; (also: COMPUTE WSI-ACCRUAL ROUNDED = WSI-ACCRUAL * WSI-DAYS)
Notes: Simple (not compound) interest: the per-diem is not re-based within the period.

Rule in plain English: The three band accruals are added into one figure for the bucket.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WSI-ACCRUAL = WSI-ACCRUAL-1 + WSI-ACCRUAL-2 + WSI-ACCRUAL-3

What it computes: Post accrual to the cash bucket
Rule in plain English: Accrued cash interest is added to the account's cash interest bucket and to the daily interest-accrual record.
COBOL as written: ADD WSI-ACCRUAL TO CM-CASH-ACCRUED-INTR ; ADD WSI-ACCRUAL TO INTM-INTACR-CSH-ACCRUED-TODAY
Notes: Cash and retail interest are accrued and held separately all the way to statement.

What it computes: Post accrual to the retail bucket
Rule in plain English: Accrued retail interest is added to the account's retail interest bucket.
COBOL as written: ADD WSI-ACCRUAL TO CM-RTL-ACCRUED-INTR ; ADD WSI-ACCRUAL TO INTM-INTACR-RTL-ACCRUED-TODAY

Rule in plain English: Cash interest is calculated only when the cash balance is positive and the account is not cash-interest-free; the same test applies to retail.
COBOL as written: IF CASH-INTR-FREE AND CASH2-INTR-FREE  NEXT SENTENCE ; ELSE IF CM-CASH-BALANCE > ZERO  PERFORM COMPUTE-CASH-INTEREST ; IF RETAIL-INTR-FREE AND RETAIL2/3-INTR-FREE  NEXT SENTENCE ; ELSE IF CM-RTL-BALANCE > ZERO  PERFORM COMPUTE-RETAIL-INTEREST
Notes: Interest-free (grace) status is per sub-bucket, not per account.

Rule in plain English: If the account is frozen for interest, or every bucket is interest-free, accrual is skipped entirely for the day.
COBOL as written: IF FREEZE-INTEREST (IBC) OR (CASH-INTR-FREE AND CASH2-INTR-FREE AND ; RETAIL-INTR-FREE AND RETAIL2-INTR-FREE AND RETAIL3-INTR-FREE) ; PERFORM UPDATE-ACCT-ANTICIPATE-DATE ... GO TO PIR-XIT-1
Notes: The accrue-through date still rolls forward, so no days are double-counted later.

Rule in plain English: The rate actually applied is the product rate plus any account-level adjustment; x100 turns it into a displayable percentage.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WSM-CBC-RATE ROUNDED = (CM-CI-RATE-1 + CM-CI-ADJ-1) * 100 ; COMPUTE WSM-CAC-RATE ROUNDED = CM-CI-RATE-2 * 100
Notes: CI- = cash interest, RI- = retail interest. Rates are held as decimal fractions.

What it computes: Total accrued interest on the account
Rule in plain English: All five interest buckets added together for reporting and for the available-credit reduction.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WS-WORK-ACCRUED-INT = CM-RTL-ACCRUED-INTR + CM-RTL2-ACCRUED-INTR ; + CM-RTL3-ACCRUED-INTR + CM-CASH-ACCRUED-INTR + CM-CASH2-ACCRUED-INTR

Rule in plain English: Balance multiplied by days is accumulated each cycle; dividing the total by the accumulated days gives the average daily balance.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE CM-AGGR-YTD-BALANCE = CM-AGGR-YTD-BALANCE ; + ((CM-CASH-BALANCE + CM-RTL-BALANCE) * WSI-DAYS) ; ADD WSI-DAYS TO CM-AGGR-YTD-DAYS
Notes: Parallel cash-only and retail-only counters exist (CM-AGGR-CASH-DAYS, CM-AGGR-RTL-DAYS).

What it computes: Interest earned on a credit balance
Rule in plain English: When the account is in credit, interest is paid to the customer: balance x credit rate x daily fraction x days. The balance is first capped at limit 3, then rate 1 or rate 2 applies depending on whether it is below limit 2.
COBOL as written: IF WSI-AMNT > TCICB-LIMIT-3  MOVE TCICB-LIMIT-3 TO WSI-AMNT ; IF WSI-AMNT < TCICB-LIMIT-2 ; COMPUTE CM-IE-ACCRUED ROUNDED = ; WSI-AMNT * TCICB-RATE-1 * WSI-DAY-FACTOR * CM-IE-AGGR-DAYS ; ELSE ; COMPUTE CM-IE-ACCRUED ROUNDED = ; WSI-AMNT * TCICB-RATE-2 * WSI-DAY-FACTOR * CM-IE-AGGR-DAYS
Notes: TCICB = interest on credit balance. The cap at limit 3 means credit interest is not paid on very large credit balances.

Rule in plain English: An accrual already taken is subtracted back out of the bucket and out of the daily accrual record.
COBOL as written: SUBTRACT WSI-ACCRUAL FROM CM-CASH-ACCRUED-INTR ; SUBTRACT WSI-ACCRUAL FROM CM-RTL-ACCRUED-INTR
Notes: Used when a payment back-dates into the accrual period, or interest is waived.

What it computes: Anticipated interest net of negative anticipation
Rule in plain English: Retail interest expected to be billed, less interest already anticipated in the other direction.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WSI-ACCRUAL-RTL = CM-RTL-ACCRUED-INTR - CM-RTL-NEG-ANTICI-INTR
Notes: Source comment notes negative anticipated balances became redundant from V2R1 onward.

Rule in plain English: Interest on a single back-dated transaction: its amount x rate x daily fraction.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WSI-ACCRUAL ROUNDED = CMT-AMNT * WSI-RATE * WSI-DAY-FACTOR

Rule in plain English: The cash-advance fee table is searched on the transaction's source code. ATM network names map to fixed source codes.
COBOL as written: MOVE CMT-SOURCE-CODE TO WS-SOURCE-CODE  (or CMT-ORIG-SOURCE-CODE if transferred) ; IF WS-SHORT-DESC = 'CIRRUS'  MOVE +0015 TO WS-SOURCE-CODE ; IF WS-SHORT-DESC = 'PLUS  '  MOVE +0014 TO WS-SOURCE-CODE ; SEARCH TC-CA-PER-TABLE WHEN TC-CA-PER-SRCE (ICAP) = WS-SOURCE-CODE
Notes: No matching row means no percentage fee is raised (AT END GO TO CAPC-EXIT).

Rule in plain English: Where the table row has no limit, the fee is simply a percentage of the advance.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WS-CA-PERCENT-CHARGE ROUNDED = ; (CMT-AMNT * TC-CA-PER-RATE-1 (ICAP)) / 100
Notes: Divide by 100 because the table holds the rate as a percentage, not a fraction.

What it computes: Banded fee — amount within the limit
Rule in plain English: If the advance is not above the band limit, rate 1 applies to the whole amount.
COBOL as written: IF CMT-AMNT NOT > TC-CA-PER-LIMIT (ICAP) ; COMPUTE WS-CA-PERCENT-CHARGE ROUNDED = ; (CMT-AMNT * TC-CA-PER-RATE-1 (ICAP)) / 100

What it computes: Banded fee — amount above the limit
Rule in plain English: Above the limit the fee is split: rate 1 on the limit, rate 2 on the excess.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WS-CA-AMNT-OVER-LIMIT = CMT-AMNT - TC-CA-PER-LIMIT (ICAP) ; COMPUTE WS-CA-PERCENT-CHARGE ROUNDED = ; ((TC-CA-PER-LIMIT (ICAP) * TC-CA-PER-RATE-1 (ICAP)) ; + (WS-CA-AMNT-OVER-LIMIT * TC-CA-PER-RATE-2 (ICAP))) / 100

Rule in plain English: The computed fee is raised to the minimum charge, or cut to the maximum charge.
COBOL as written: IF WS-CA-PERCENT-CHARGE < TC-CA-PERCENT-MIN-CHRG ; MOVE TC-CA-PERCENT-MIN-CHRG TO WS-CA-PERCENT-CHARGE ; IF WS-CA-PERCENT-CHARGE > TC-CA-PERCENT-MAX-CHRG ; MOVE TC-CA-PERCENT-MAX-CHRG TO WS-CA-PERCENT-CHARGE
Notes: This is the classic 'x% of the advance, minimum RMn' rule.

Rule in plain English: The fee is posted as its own transaction, into the cash bucket.
COBOL as written: PERFORM GENERATE-BASIC-TRANS ; MOVE 3700 TO GT-TRANS-CODE GT-TRANS-TYPE ; MOVE 'CSH1' TO GT-BAL-BUCKET ; MOVE WS-CA-PERCENT-CHARGE TO GT-AMNT
Notes: Posting to CSH1 means the fee itself then attracts cash-rate interest.

Rule in plain English: Cash exposure = posted cash balance plus outstanding cash authorisations, less over-limit payments already credited.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE ACR-CM-CASHBAL-AUTH = ; CM-CASH-BALANCE + CM-CASH-ADV-OS-AUTH - CM-OL-CASH-PYMT

What it computes: Balance the late fee is measured on
Rule in plain English: The late-fee base is the opening (beginning) balance of the cycle, retail plus cash.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE CM-STMT-BAL-FOR-LATE-FEE = ; CM-RTL-BEG-BALANCE + CM-CASH-BEG-BALANCE

Rule in plain English: No late charge is raised if the account or product waives it. If the base balance is zero or below, the accrued late-charge buckets are cleared.
COBOL as written: IF WAIVE-LATE-CHARGES OR TC-WAIVE-LATE-CHRG (IBC)  GO TO LCP-XIT ; IF CM-STMT-BAL-FOR-LATE-FEE <= ZEROS ; MOVE ZEROES TO CM-ACCR-LATE-CHG-CTD CM-ACCR-LATE-CHG-BNP

What it computes: Flat fee plus percentage of unpaid balance (flag 2)
Rule in plain English: A fixed charge plus a percentage of the unpaid statement balances across all retail, cash and insurance buckets.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WS-AMNT ROUNDED = TCM-LATE-CHARGE + ; ((CM-RTL1-BALANCE-STMT + CM-CASH1-BALANCE-STMT ; + CM-RTL2-BALANCE-STMT + CM-CASH2-BALANCE-STMT ; + CM-RTL3-BALANCE-STMT + CM-RTL-INSUR-BNP) * TCM-LC-PERCENT)

Rule in plain English: A single fixed late charge, regardless of balance.
COBOL as written: IF TCF-LATE-CHARGE-FLAG IS EQUAL TO 0 OR 5 ; COMPUTE WS-AMNT ROUNDED = TCM-LATE-CHARGE

What it computes: Flat fee plus percentage of total unpaid
Rule in plain English: Variant that applies the percentage to a single total-unpaid figure.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WS-AMNT ROUNDED = ; TCM-LATE-CHARGE + (WS-TOT-UNPAID-BAL * TCM-LC-PERCENT)

Rule in plain English: How far the posted balance exceeds the credit limit.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE CPCT-AMT-OVERLIMIT = ; CM-RTL-BALANCE + CM-CASH-BALANCE - CM-CRLIMIT

What it computes: Over-limit amount added to amount due
Rule in plain English: Any new over-limit excess not already demanded is added to the over-limit amount due.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WS-AMNT = (CM-CURR-BALANCE - CM-CRLIMIT) - CM-OL-AMT-DUE ; COMPUTE CM-OL-AMT-DUE = CM-OL-AMT-DUE + WS-AMNT

What it computes: Cash limit derived from credit limit
Rule in plain English: The cash limit is a set percentage of the overall credit limit.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE CM-CASH-LIMIT ROUNDED = TCM-CASH-LIMIT-PERCENT * CM-CRLIMIT

What it computes: Instalment limit derived from credit limit
Rule in plain English: The instalment limit is a set percentage of the overall credit limit.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE CM-INSTL-LIMIT ROUNDED = TCM-INSTL-LIMIT-PERCENT * CM-CRLIMIT

Rule in plain English: Limit (grossed up by the permitted over-limit factor) less what is used, less outstanding authorisations, plus over-limit payments received.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE CM-AVAIL-CREDIT ROUNDED = ; (CM-CRLIMIT * TCM-OVER-LIMIT) - CM-CURR-BALANCE ; - CM-AMNT-OUTST-AUTH + CM-OL-CASH-PYMT + CM-OL-RTL-PYMT
Notes: TCM-OVER-LIMIT is a multiplier (e.g. 1.10 for a 10% tolerance), not an amount.

Rule in plain English: Cash limit grossed up by the over-limit factor, less cash balance and outstanding cash authorisations.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE CM-AVAIL-CASH ROUNDED = ; CM-CASH-LIMIT * TCM-OVER-LIMIT - CM-CASH-BALANCE ; - CM-CASH-ADV-OS-AUTH + CM-OL-CASH-PYMT

Rule in plain English: Instalment limit less instalment balance and outstanding instalment authorisations.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE CM-AVAIL-INSTL ROUNDED = ; CM-INSTL-LIMIT - CM-INSTL-BAL - CM-AMNT-OUTST-INSTL

What it computes: Instalment balance reserved against available credit
Rule in plain English: Only a configured share of the instalment balance is held back from the main available credit.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE CM-AVAIL-CREDIT = ; CM-AVAIL-CREDIT - (TC-INSTL-EM-AVL-PER * CM-INSTL-BAL)

What it computes: Available credit net of accrued interest
Rule in plain English: Unbilled accrued interest is deducted from available credit so the customer cannot spend it.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE CM-AVAIL-CREDIT ROUNDED = (WS-AMNT ; - CM-RTL-ACCRUED-INTR - CM-RTL2-ACCRUED-INTR - CM-RTL3-ACCRUED-INTR ; - CM-CASH-ACCRUED-INTR - CM-CASH2-ACCRUED-INTR)

Rule in plain English: Debits as a proportion of the credit limit, scaled to one decimal place of a percentage.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WS-CREDIT-LIMIT-USG = (WS-USER-AMT-DEBITS / CM-CRLIMIT) * 1000 ; COMPUTE CESF01-CRLIMIT-USG-TODAY = WS-CREDIT-LIMIT-USG / 10
Notes: x1000 then /10 preserves one decimal in integer arithmetic.

Rule in plain English: Where the product bills in full, the amount due is simply the current balance.
COBOL as written: IF BILL-TOTAL-BALANCE  MOVE CM-CURR-BALANCE TO WS-PYMT
Notes: Charge cards and some corporate products use this.

Rule in plain English: A pre-set fixed instalment is billed instead of a percentage.
COBOL as written: IF BILL-FIXED-AMNT AND CM-FIXED-PYMT-AMNT > ZERO ; MOVE CM-FIXED-PYMT-AMNT TO WS-PYMT

What it computes: Derive the fixed amount from principal
Rule in plain English: The fixed payment is a percentage of principal, where principal excludes disputed balances and billed charges.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WS-PRINCIPAL-AMOUNT EQUAL CM-CURR-BALANCE ; - CM-CASH-DISPUTED-BAL - CM-RTL-DISPUTED-BAL - WS-PRINCIPAL-CHARGES ; COMPUTE CM-FIXED-PYMT-AMNT ROUNDED EQUAL ; WS-PRINCIPAL-AMOUNT * TCP-PERCENT (ITCP)
Notes: TCP-PERCENT is picked from a table band (ITCP) — high balance, reducing, or new-debit method.

Rule in plain English: Only interest held plus charges and billed interest fees are demanded.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WS-PYMT = WS-RTL-ACCR-HOLD + WS-CASH-ACCR-HOLD ; + WS-RTL-CHRG + WS-CASH-CHRG + WS-BILL-INTR-FEES

What it computes: Split into bill-in-full and revolving parts
Rule in plain English: Balances are split: WS-PYMT1 is billed in full (fees, instalment due), WS-PYMT2 is the revolving remainder.
COBOL as written: MOVE ZEROES TO WS-PYMT1 WS-PYMT2 ; PERFORM BAL-BUCKET-BILL-FULL ; ADD CM-CTD-IPP-BALANCE TO WS-PYMT1 ; SUBTRACT CM-CTD-IPP-BALANCE FROM WS-PYMT2 ; SUBTRACT CM-PCB-IPP-BALANCE FROM WS-PYMT2
Notes: IPP = instalment payment plan; its current due is always billed in full.

Rule in plain English: Where the derive method is zero, the revolving part is divided by the payment term.
COBOL as written: IF TCM-DERIVE-METHOD = ZERO ; COMPUTE WS-PYMT ROUNDED = WS-PYMT1 + WS-PYMT2 / TCM-PAYMENT-TERM
Notes: E.g. a term of 20 bills 1/20th = 5% of the revolving balance.

Rule in plain English: Otherwise the revolving part is multiplied by the payment term treated as a percentage.
COBOL as written: ELSE ; COMPUTE WS-PYMT ROUNDED = ; WS-PYMT1 + WS-PYMT2 * TCM-PAYMENT-TERM / 100
Notes: E.g. a term of 5 bills 5% of the revolving balance.

Rule in plain English: If the revolving remainder is negative it is added as-is rather than being scaled.
COBOL as written: IF WS-PYMT2 < ZERO ; COMPUTE WS-PYMT = WS-PYMT1 + WS-PYMT2

What it computes: Bill the whole balance when no term is set
Rule in plain English: A zero payment term with a zero derive method means the full balance is demanded.
COBOL as written: IF TCM-PAYMENT-TERM = ZERO AND TCM-DERIVE-METHOD = ZERO ; MOVE CM-CURR-BALANCE TO WS-PYMT

Rule in plain English: If the computed amount is below the product minimum, the minimum is used — unless the balance is under the threshold, or the card is interest-only, budget or fixed-term-loan.
COBOL as written: IF BILL-INTEREST-ONLY OR CM-CURR-BALANCE NOT > TCM-PYMT-THRESHOLD ; NEXT SENTENCE ; ELSE IF (WS-PYMT < TCM-MINIMUM-PYMT) ; AND NOT BUDGET-CARD AND NOT FIXED-TERM-LOAN-CARD ; MOVE TCM-MINIMUM-PYMT TO WS-PYMT
Notes: This is the 'or RMn, whichever is higher' clause on a statement.

What it computes: Round up to whole currency units
Rule in plain English: Where the product bills in even dollars, .99 is added and the result truncated — i.e. rounded up.
COBOL as written: IF BILL-EVEN-DOLLARS ; ADD .99 TO WS-PYMT ; MOVE WS-PYMT TO WS-DOLLARS ; MOVE WS-DOLLARS TO WS-PYMT
Notes: WS-DOLLARS has no decimal places, so the MOVE truncates.

Rule in plain English: If the balance is over the limit and the product demands all of it, the whole excess is added on top of the minimum.
COBOL as written: IF CM-CURR-BALANCE > CM-CRLIMIT AND BILL-ALL-OVER-LIMIT ; COMPUTE WS-PYMT = WS-PYMT + (CM-CURR-BALANCE - CM-CRLIMIT)

Rule in plain English: Transactions up to the free/banded limit are charged at rate 1, the rest at rate 2.
COBOL as written: IF TCSC-LIMIT (ISC) > ZERO AND WS-COUNT > TCSC-LIMIT (ISC) ; COMPUTE WS-CHRG = ; (TCSC-LIMIT (ISC) * TCSC-RATE-1 (ISC)) ; + ((WS-COUNT - TCSC-LIMIT (ISC)) * TCSC-RATE-2 (ISC))
Notes: WS-COUNT is the transaction count for the bucket, not an amount.

Rule in plain English: With no band, every transaction is charged at rate 1.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WS-CHRG = WS-COUNT * TCSC-RATE-1 (ISC)

What it computes: Split the charge to retail or cash
Rule in plain English: The charge lands in the retail or the cash bucket depending on the service-charge type.
COBOL as written: IF TSC-RETAIL (ISC)  ADD WS-CHRG TO WS-RTL-CHRG ; ELSE  ADD WS-CHRG TO WS-CASH-CHRG

Rule in plain English: Retail and cash charges are totalled; if the total breaches the maximum, the bucket currently being processed is cut back so that the two together equal the cap.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WS-AMNT = WS-RTL-CHRG + WS-CASH-CHRG ; IF (WS-AMNT > TCSC-MAXIMUM) ; IF (TSC-RETAIL (ISC)) ; COMPUTE WS-RTL-CHRG = TCSC-MAXIMUM - WS-CASH-CHRG ; ELSE ; COMPUTE WS-CASH-CHRG = TCSC-MAXIMUM - WS-RTL-CHRG
Notes: The cap is on the combined charge, not per bucket. WS-MAX-TR-SW is set to flag that the cap was hit.

Rule in plain English: Retail plus cash balances, less amounts under dispute.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE CM-CURR-BALANCE = CM-RTL-BALANCE + CM-CASH-BALANCE ; - CM-RTL-DISPUTED-BAL - CM-CASH-DISPUTED-BAL
Notes: Disputed amounts are excluded from the balance the customer is asked to pay.

Rule in plain English: A simple retail plus cash total used earlier in the cycle.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE CM-CURR-BALANCE = CM-CASH-BALANCE + CM-RTL-BALANCE

Rule in plain English: The three retail sub-buckets are summed into the retail total.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE CM-RTL-CURR-MON-BAL = CM-RTL1-CURR-MON-BAL ; + CM-RTL2-CURR-MON-BAL + CM-RTL3-CURR-MON-BAL
Notes: Sub-buckets carry different interest rates, which is why they are held apart.

Rule in plain English: The statement balance is the ledger balance less interest, service, misc, insurance and membership amounts that are billed but not yet posted.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE CM-RTL1-BALANCE-STMT = CM-RTL1-BALANCE ; - (CM-RTL-IBNP + CM-RTL-SVC-BNP + CM-RTL-MISC-FEES ; + CM-RTL-INSUR-BNP + CM-RTL-MEMBER-BNP + CM-RTL1-FEE)
Notes: BNP = billed not posted. IBNP = interest billed not posted.

Rule in plain English: Same treatment on the cash side.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE CM-CASH1-BALANCE-STMT = CM-CASH1-BALANCE ; - (CM-CASH-IBNP + CM-CASH-SVC-BNP + CM-CASH1-FEE)

Rule in plain English: Retail and cash statement balances totalled for presentation.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WS-RTL-STMT-BAL = CM-RTL1-BALANCE-STMT ; + CM-RTL2-BALANCE-STMT + CM-RTL3-BALANCE-STMT ; COMPUTE WS-CASH-STMT-BAL = CM-CASH1-BALANCE-STMT + CM-CASH2-BALANCE-STMT

What it computes: Prior month closing principal and interest
Rule in plain English: At cycle close the principal (balance plus instalment balance) and the accrued interest are snapshotted.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE CM-PREV-MTH-CLOSE-PRIN = CM-CURR-BALANCE + CM-INSTL-BAL ; COMPUTE CM-PREV-MTH-CLOSE-INTR ROUNDED = ; CM-CASH-ACCRUED-INTR + CM-CASH2-ACCRUED-INTR (+ retail terms)

What it computes: Bonus points earned in the cycle
Rule in plain English: Net qualifying retail spend — debits less miscellaneous charges, less the annual fee, less non-payment credits — multiplied by the bonus rate.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WS-BONUS-BUCKS-EARNED ROUNDED = ; ((CM-RTL-AMNT-DB - CM-RTL-MISC-CTD) - WS-TEMP-ANN-FEE ; - (CM-RTL-AMNT-CR - CM-RTL-PYMT-CTD)) * TCM-BONUS-PERCENT
Notes: Refunds reduce earned points; payments do not, which is why payments are added back.

Rule in plain English: Opening bonus balance plus points earned less points redeemed in the cycle.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE CM-BB-BEG-BALANCE = CM-BB-BEG-BALANCE ; + WS-BONUS-BUCKS-EARNED - CM-BB-USED-CTD

Rule in plain English: Cashback arrives in minor units and is rescaled to the destination currency's decimal convention.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WS-AMT = ; (CXVSA-FIN-TCR1-CASHBACK / 100) * (10 ** WS-DST-CCY-EXP)

What it computes: Merchant rebate in the daily settlement
Rule in plain English: Merchant rebate fees are added back when the merchant's carried-forward balance is struck.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WS-TOT-AMT-MER-RB-FEE = MAR-CAC-REBATE-FEE (WS-SUB)

Rule in plain English: Tax is the discount amount multiplied by the GST rate held on the transaction, divided by 100.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WT-BDE-T-ENR-GST-AMT ROUNDED = ; CQBDTE-T-ENR-DIS-AMT * CQBDTE-T-GST-RTE / 100
Notes: The rate travels on the transaction record, so a rate change applies from its effective date.

What it computes: Daily discount GST net of enrolment GST
Rule in plain English: Total discount GST for the day less the GST already taken on enrolment fees.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WS-DLY-DISC-GST = WS-TOT-DISC-GST ; - WT-MCC-ENR-GST-AMT - WT-MCD-ENR-GST-AMT - WT-MPR-ENR-GST-AMT

What it computes: Net sales grossed up by enrolment GST
Rule in plain English: Enrolment GST is added back into net sales so the settlement figure reconciles.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WS-DLY-NET-SALES = WS-TOT-NET-SALES ; + WT-MCC-ENR-GST-AMT + WT-MCD-ENR-GST-AMT + WT-MPR-ENR-GST-AMT

What it computes: GST sign reversal on the statement detail
Rule in plain English: GST is flipped in sign when written to the merchant statement detail record.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE MSTD1-GST-AMT = WT-BDE-T-DIS-GST-AMT * -1 ; COMPUTE MSAD1-GST-AMT = CQBDTE-T-FEE-GST-AMT * -1
Notes: Fees are debits to the merchant, hence the sign flip for presentation.

What it computes: Interest expense to the YTD tax buckets
Rule in plain English: Interest paid is accumulated into calendar and fiscal year-to-date buckets for tax reporting.
COBOL as written: ADD CMT-AMNT TO CM-IE-YTD CM-IE-TAX-YTD ; OC-INTEREST-PAID-CALENDAR-YTD OC-INTEREST-PAID-FISCAL-YTD

Rule in plain English: Total discount divided by the card count gives the average rate for the merchant.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WS-AVG-DISC-RATE = WS-TOT-DISC / WS-CARD-COUNT
Notes: Guard: only reached when WS-CARD-COUNT is non-zero.

Rule in plain English: The average rate is reduced by a concession looked up on discount type, sales band and range.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WS-DISC-RATE = WS-AVG-DISC-RATE ; - OCMDM-PCT-UNDER-BASE-RATE (X-OCM-DISC, X-OCM-SALES, X-OCM-RANGE)
Notes: Three-dimensional table: higher volume earns a bigger reduction.

What it computes: Discount amount charged to the merchant
Rule in plain English: Fee-based sales multiplied by the effective discount rate.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE MMD-AMT-DISC (1) ROUNDED = ; WS-AMT-FEE-BASED-SALES * WS-DISC-RATE

Rule in plain English: Each sales band's amount is rated separately and added to the running discount.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE MMD-AMT-DISC (1) ROUNDED = ; MMD-AMT-DISC (1) + (WS-FBS-AMNT * WS-DISC-RATE)

Rule in plain English: The blended rate actually charged, derived from the discount taken over the sales it was taken on.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WS-DISC-RATE = MMD-AMT-DISC (1) / WS-AMT-FEE-BASED-SALES
Notes: Used for the rate shown on the merchant statement.

Rule in plain English: Sales less returns across all card schemes gives the amount to pay the merchant.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WS-SALES = ; MMD-VI-AMT-TOTAL-SALES (1) - MMD-VI-AMT-TOTAL-RETURNS (1) ; + MMD-MC-... + MMD-JCB-... (per scheme) ; COMPUTE CPWMMR-MK4-ACH-AMOUNT = WS-SALES * -1
Notes: Sign is flipped for the outgoing payment instruction.

What it computes: Discount and fees withheld from settlement
Rule in plain English: Discount plus fees are settled as a separate ACH debit.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE CPWMMR-MK4-ACH-AMOUNT = (MMD-AMT-DISC (2) + MMD-AMT-FEES (2))

Rule in plain English: Opening balance plus net sales and payment adjustments, less adjustments, fees and fee GST, plus rebates.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE MAR-BALANCE-CF = MAR-BALANCE-BF + WS-TOT-NET-SALES ; + WS-TOT-PAYMENT-ADJ - WS-TOT-ADJUSTMENT - WS-TOT-FEES ; - WS-TOT-FEES-GST + WS-TOT-AMT-MER-RB-FEE + WS-AMT-REBATE
Notes: The merchant accounting equivalent of a statement roll-forward.

Rule in plain English: A per-item fee times the item count, plus an ad-valorem rate times the amount — both looked up by acquirer region, issuer region and programme.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WS-MC-NFI-FEE (lvl) = ; (WS-MC-NFI-NBR (lvl) * WS-ICG-RTL-PGM-ITEM (acq, iss, pgm)) ; + (WS-MC-NFI-AMT (lvl) * WS-ICG-RTL-PGM-RATE (acq, iss, pgm))
Notes: The standard scheme interchange shape: fixed per transaction plus a percentage.

Rule in plain English: The interchange figure is negated to express it as a cost.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WS-MC-BATCH-INTCHG-FEE ROUNDED = WS-MC-SI-AMT3 * -1.00

Rule in plain English: Cash advance and ATM amounts are folded into the batch net.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WS-MC-BATCH-NET-AMT = WS-MC-BATCH-NET-AMT ; + WS-MC-BATCH-AMT-CASH-ADV + WS-MC-BATCH-AMT-ATM

Rule in plain English: Net plus interchange, cash advance and ATM fees gives the settlement figure for the batch.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WS-MC-BATCH-AMT = WS-MC-BATCH-NET-AMT ; + WS-MC-BATCH-INTCHG-FEE + WS-MC-BATCH-FEE-CASH-ADV ; + WS-MC-BATCH-FEE-ATM

Rule in plain English: Scheme interchange rates are held on the organisation control record and maintained by percentage or absolute change.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE FM1-NO-47-VISA-INTCHG-RATE (i) = ; OCM-VISA-INTCHG-RATE (j) * WS-PERCENT-HOLD ; (or + / - WSCPS-MAINT-FIELD-NUMERIC)
Notes: CPU600 is the mass-maintenance program; it changes the rates the batch then applies.

Rule in plain English: Visa carries amounts in minor units with a currency exponent; the amount is divided by 100 and rescaled by 10 to the power of that exponent.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WS-AMT = ; (CXVSA-DSP-TCR1-DEST-AMT / 100) * (10 ** WS-DST-CCY-EXP)
Notes: Handles currencies with 0, 2 or 3 decimal places from one wire format.

What it computes: Visa conversion rate is read, not computed
Rule in plain English: The Visa rate is read once from the VISRATE file at the start of the run and held for the whole job. An empty file is fatal — the program abends rather than convert at a wrong rate.
COBOL as written: OBTAIN-VISA-CURRENCY-RATE. ; OPEN INPUT VMC-CURRENCY-RATE-FILE ; READ VMC-CURRENCY-RATE-FILE ; AT END MOVE 88888 TO WS-ABEND-CODE ; MOVE 'VISRATE FILE IS EMPTY' TO WS-ABENDMSG ; PERFORM ZZZZ-ABEND ; MOVE VMC-VISA-RATE TO WS-VISA-RATE ; CLOSE VMC-CURRENCY-RATE-FILE
Notes: Rate maintenance is a data change, not a code change. NOTE: the older CPRTB currency-rate-table path (WS-IN-ORG-RATE = CPRTB-INCOM-RATE / 10**exponent, and cash fee rate = rate * 0.99) is commented out in CALC-CURR-CONV-RATE and in CPD030 - do not mistake it for live logic.

What it computes: Months on which interest is payable
Rule in plain English: Repayment term less the interest-free period.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WS-FTL-MNTHS-INT-PAYABLE = ; (CMA-FTL-REPAYMENT-TERM - CMA-FTL-INT-FREE-PERIOD)

What it computes: Insurance premium share of the instalment
Rule in plain English: The premium's share of the instalment due, pro-rated by premium over premium plus principal.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WS-AMNT4 = ((WS-FTL-TOT-DUE-TD - WS-FTL-TOT-INT-TD) ; * (CMA-FTL-INS-PREMIUM ; / (CMA-FTL-INS-PREMIUM + WS-FTL-TOT-PRNCPL-AMNT)))

Rule in plain English: The four principal tranches added together.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE CRR-R45-PRINCIPAL-AMT = (CMA-FTL-LOAN-PRNCPL1 ; + CMA-FTL-LOAN-PRNCPL2 + CMA-FTL-LOAN-PRNCPL3 + CMA-FTL-LOAN-PRNCPL4)

Rule in plain English: Instalment balance plus outstanding instalment authorisations.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE ACR-INSTL-BAL = CM-INSTL-BAL + CM-AMNT-OUTST-INSTL

Rule in plain English: Credit used is increased by the configured share of the instalment balance.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE ACR-CREDIT-USED = ACR-CREDIT-USED ; + (TC-INSTL-EM-AVL-PER * CM-INSTL-BAL)

Rule in plain English: Provisional interest less negative provisional interest, accumulated for the general ledger.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WST-PROVISIONAL ROUNDED = WST-PROVISIONAL ; + CM-RTL-PROVIS-INTR - CM-RTL-NEG-PROVIS-INTR
Notes: CPD110B1 carries the same computation over the ABP (account balance process) record.

Rule in plain English: Daily fraction times the provisional retail balance times the rate.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WSP-INT ROUNDED = ; WSI-DAY-FACTOR * WSP-RTL-PROVIS-BAL * WSI-RATE-1
Notes: Suspended interest on delinquent accounts: accrued but not taken to income.

Rule in plain English: Bad-debt, bankruptcy, fraud and counterfeit write-offs added into one gross charge-off figure.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WSS117-CQ-AX3F-GROSS-CHGOFF (n) = ; ...BDEBT-WTEOFF + ...BKRUPT-WTEOFF ; + ...FRAUD-LOSSES + ...CTFEIT-LOSSES + ...
Notes: Feeds the quarterly affiliation / regulatory schedule.

What it computes: Interest activity to the general ledger
Rule in plain English: Each accrual is mirrored to a GL amount and posted through the cardholder GL routine.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WS-AMOUNT-GL ROUNDED = WSI-ACCRUAL ; PERFORM GENERATE-INT-ACTIV-GL / GGTG-UPD-CARDH-GL
Notes: Keeps the subsidiary ledger and the GL in step day by day.

What it computes: Rounding to the cent on GL transactions
Rule in plain English: Half a cent is added before the amount is moved to the transaction field, giving round-half-up.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE GT-AMNT = WSI-ACCRUAL + .005
Notes: The receiving field has two decimals, so the MOVE truncates the rest.

Rule in plain English: The financed item price divided by the number of payment terms gives the monthly instalment.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WS-MERCH-ADJ-AMT ROUNDED = EPT-ITEM-PRICE / EPT-PAY-TERM
Notes: Easy Payment Plan. The merchant adjustment is the subsidy the merchant funds.

Rule in plain English: The monthly amount multiplied by the number of months in the waiver window, inclusive of both ends.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WS-MERCH-ADJ-AMT = ; WS-MERCH-ADJ-AMT * (EPT-WAIVE-TO-MOS - EPT-WAIVE-FR-MOS + 1)
Notes: The +1 makes the range inclusive — months 3 to 6 is four months, not three.

What it computes: Instalment billed during the interest-free window
Rule in plain English: Inside the interest-free months the billed amount is the standard instalment less the interest element, so only principal is demanded.
COBOL as written: IF EPT-INTR-FREE-MOS > 0 ; IF EPT-PAID-TERMS > EPT-INTR-FREE-MOS ; MOVE EPT-MON-INSTL-AMT TO EPGTF-TRANS-AMOUNT ; ELSE IF EPT-PAID-TERMS = 1 ; MOVE EPT-FIRST-PAY-AMT TO EPGTF-TRANS-AMOUNT ; ELSE ; COMPUTE EPGTF-TRANS-AMOUNT = EPT-MON-INSTL-AMT - WS-INTEREST-TEMP
Notes: The first instalment uses EPT-FIRST-PAY-AMT, which may differ from later ones.

Rule in plain English: The instalment less its interest element is the principal repaid this month.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE EPGTF-PRIN-AMOUNT = EPGTF-TRANS-AMOUNT - WS-INTEREST
Notes: Standard amortisation split: interest first, the rest reduces principal.

Rule in plain English: Outstanding principal is reduced by the principal repaid, and outstanding interest by the interest taken.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE EPT-OUTS-PRINCIPAL = EPT-OUTS-PRINCIPAL - EPGTF-PRIN-AMOUNT ; SUBTRACT WS-INTEREST FROM EPT-OUTS-INT
Notes: Principal and interest are tracked as separate outstanding balances throughout the plan.

Rule in plain English: Settling early demands the whole outstanding principal plus the outstanding interest.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE EPGTF-TRANS-AMOUNT = EPT-OUTS-PRINCIPAL + EPT-OUTS-INT
Notes: Whether unearned interest is rebated is a product decision, not visible in this statement alone.

Rule in plain English: When a payment must be split across retail and cash, the retail share is retail's proportion of the two statement balances.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WS-TEMP-RATE ROUNDED = ; WS-RTL-STMT-BAL / (WS-CASH-STMT-BAL + WS-RTL-STMT-BAL)
Notes: Only applied when both balances are above zero; otherwise the payment goes wholly to the non-zero side.

Rule in plain English: The payment multiplied by the retail proportion is posted to retail.
COBOL as written: MOVE WS-PYMT TO WS-SAVE-PYMT ; COMPUTE WS-PYMT ROUNDED = WS-SAVE-PYMT * WS-TEMP-RATE

Rule in plain English: Whatever is left after the retail share is posted to the cash balance, so nothing is lost to rounding.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WS-SAVE-PYMT = WS-SAVE-PYMT - WS-PYMT ; PERFORM PPT-RTL-STMT-BAL ; MOVE WS-SAVE-PYMT TO WS-PYMT ; PERFORM PPT-CASH-STMT-BAL
Notes: Taking the remainder rather than a second multiplication is what keeps the two halves summing to the payment.

Rule in plain English: The same proportional split, applied to current-month balances when the payment exceeds the statement balances.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WS-TEMP-RATE ROUNDED = ; CM-RTL-CURR-MON-BAL / (CM-CASH-CURR-MON-BAL + CM-RTL-CURR-MON-BAL)
Notes: Statement balances are cleared first, then current-month balances.

Rule in plain English: Opening balance plus transfers in and accruals and debit adjustments, less transfers out, credit adjustments and waivers, gives the closing bucket.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE TCAI-ENDING-BALANCE (IAI) = ; TCAI-BEG-BALANCE (IAI) + TCAI-TRANSFER-IN (IAI) ; - TCAI-TRANSFER-OUT (IAI) + TCAI-ACCRUED (IAI) ; + TCAI-DEBIT-ADJUST (IAI) - TCAI-CREDIT-ADJUST (IAI) - ...
Notes: CPD810 merges CPD110's updates into CPQAF. A parallel set of CO- fields tracks charged-off accounts.

Rule in plain English: The same roll-forward for suspended (provisional) interest, including movements to anticipated and waivers.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE TCPI-ENDING-BALANCE = TCPI-BEG-BALANCE + TCPI-ACCRUED ; - TCPI-NEG-ACCRUED + TCPI-TRANSFER-IN - TCPI-TO-ANTICI ; - TCPI-WAIVED + TCPI-NEG-WAIVED - TCPI-TRANSFER-OUT

Rule in plain English: The independently accumulated total is compared with the rolled-forward bucket; a non-zero difference is the control break.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WS-AMNT = ; WST-ENDING-ACCRUED (WS-TA-IDX) - TCAI-ENDING-BALANCE (IAI)
Notes: This is the out-of-balance detector for interest. A non-zero result is what an operator investigates.

Rule in plain English: Organisation-level closing balance: opening plus interest and transfers in and debits, less transfers out, charge-offs and credits.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WS-WORK-AMT = WS-ORG-BEG-BAL + WS-ORG-INTEREST ; + WS-ORG-TRNSF-IN - WS-ORG-TRNSF-OUT - WS-REG-CHGOFFS ; + WS-TOT-AMT-DB - WS-TOT-AMT-CR

Rule in plain English: The same roll-forward on the charged-off side, where charge-offs add to rather than reduce the balance.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WS-CO-WORK-AMT = WS-CO-ORG-BEG-BAL + WS-CO-ORG-INTEREST ; + WS-CO-CHGOFFS + WS-CO-TOT-AMT-DB + WS-CO-ORG-TRNSF-IN ; - WS-CO-ORG-TRNSF-OUT - WS-CO-TOT-AMT-CR
Notes: Note the sign on charge-offs is opposite to the regular portfolio — they move balance between the two.

Rule in plain English: Purchase, quasi-cash and chargeback fees are netted into one posting amount per GL category.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WS-TOT-AMT = WS-LOC-ACQ-PURC-FEE + WS-LOC-ACQ-QUASI-FEE ; + WS-LOC-ACQ-CB-FEE + WS-LOC-ACQ-QUASI-CB-FEE ; - WS-LOC-ACQ-CB-R-FEE - WS-LOC-ACQ-QUASI-CB-R-FEE
Notes: LOC = local, INT = international; ACQ = acquiring, ISS = issuing. CB-R is chargeback reversal.

What it computes: Scale the GL amount to posting currency
Rule in plain English: The settlement amount is rescaled by ten to the power of the posting currency's exponent before it is written to the GL.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WS-TOT-AMT = (WS-TOT-AMT * (10 ** CSNGL-GL-POST-CURR-EXP))
Notes: Same mechanism in CP615110. Lets one GL interface serve currencies with different decimal places.

Rule in plain English: Purchases, quasi-cash, manual and reversal amounts netted against returns for the GL entry.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WS-TOT-AMT = WS-LOC-ACQ-PURC + WS-LOC-ACQ-QUASI ; + WS-LOC-ACQ-MANUAL + WS-LOC-ACQ-PURC-REV-RTN ; - WS-LOC-ACQ-PURC-RTN

Rule in plain English: Scheme files carry amounts in minor units (cents); multiplying by 0.01 converts them to the major unit before reporting.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE MERCON-VI-AMT-NET-SALES (1) = ; MERCON-VI-AMT-NET-SALES (1) * 0.01
Notes: Applied field by field across every scheme and amount category — 120 such statements in this program alone.

Rule in plain English: Cashback is divided by ten to the power of the transaction currency's exponent, or by 100 where no exponent applies.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE CXSTX-D-CASHBACK-AMT = WS-ADD-AMT / (10 ** CXS120-TXN-CCY-EXP) ; (else) COMPUTE CXSTX-D-CASHBACK-AMT = WS-ADD-AMT / 100

What it computes: Cash rebate at a flat rate
Rule in plain English: A flat one percent of the transaction amount is credited as cash rebate.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WS-CASH-REBATE ROUNDED = LF-OUTPUT-AMOUNT * 0.0100
Notes: The 0.0100 rate is hard-coded in this program rather than table-driven — worth noting for any rate change.

Rule in plain English: The merchant discount rebate is negated for the output record, expressing it as a credit.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE LF-OUTPUT-MDR-REBATE = LF-OUTPUT-MDR-REBATE * -1

Rule in plain English: A percentage increase is turned into a multiplier by dividing by 100 and adding one, then applied to the current value.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WS-PERCENT-HOLD = (WSCPS-MAINT-FIELD-NUMERIC-R (WS-MAINT) / 100) + 1 ; COMPUTE FM1-NH-01-CREDIT-LIMIT = CUR-AMOUNT-OUT * WS-PERCENT-HOLD
Notes: A 10% rise becomes a multiplier of 1.10. This is how bulk limit and rate changes are applied.

Rule in plain English: A percentage decrease becomes one minus the fraction.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WS-PERCENT-HOLD = 1 - (WSCPS-MAINT-FIELD-NUMERIC-R (WS-MAINT) / 100)

Rule in plain English: Where the change is an amount rather than a percentage it is simply added to or subtracted from the current value.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE FM1-NH-01-CREDIT-LIMIT = ; CUR-AMOUNT-OUT + WSCPS-MAINT-FIELD-NUMERIC-R (WS-MAINT) ; (or - for a decrease)

Rule in plain English: During an authorisation enquiry the instalment share of the requested amount is deducted from available credit before the decision.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE CM-AVAIL-CREDIT ROUNDED = CM-AVAIL-CREDIT ; - (AUIS-INQ-AMOUNT-SAVE-AREA * SEC-TC-INSTL-EM-AVL-PER)
Notes: Parallel forms exist for customer level (CR-AVAIL-CREDIT) and corporate level (CORP-CR-AVAIL-CREDIT).

What it computes: Release the reserve after the decision
Rule in plain English: The same instalment reserve is added back once the enquiry amount no longer applies.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE CM-AVAIL-CREDIT ROUNDED = CM-AVAIL-CREDIT ; + (AUIS-INQ-AMOUNT-SAVE-AREA * TC-INSTL-EM-AVL-PER)

Rule in plain English: Sales amount divided by sales count gives the average ticket, computed separately for international, domestic and out-of-scheme.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE QMMRSTA-SLE-ITL-TKT (1) = ; QMMRSTA-SLE-ITL-AMT (1) / QMMRSTA-SLE-ITL-NBR (1)
Notes: Each divide is guarded by a non-zero count test.

Rule in plain English: Daily international, domestic and out-of-scheme amounts summed to the total.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE QMMRSTA-SLE-TTL-AMT (1) = ; (QMMSTAT-DLY-ITL-AMT + QMMSTAT-DLY-DOM-AMT + QMMSTAT-DLY-OUS-AMT)

What it computes: Repayment as a percentage of balance
Rule in plain English: The payment received expressed as a percentage of the current balance.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WS-REPAY-PERCENT ROUNDED = ; (BNSTRN-AMT / BNS105-CURR-BALANCE (2)) * 100
Notes: Used to classify payment behaviour — full, partial or minimum payer.

Rule in plain English: Sales less returns (or plus returns, depending on how the product treats refunds) gives the base the discount is charged on.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WS-AMT-FEE-BASED-SALES = ; MPL-PL-AMT-TOTAL-SALES (2) - MPL-PL-AMT-TOTAL-RETURNS (2) ; (or + MPL-PL-AMT-TOTAL-RETURNS (2))
Notes: Whether returns reduce or add to the fee base is a configured choice, and it changes what the merchant pays.

Rule in plain English: Outgoing (non-local) sales are removed so that local and international volumes can be priced differently.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WS-AMT-LOCAL-FEE-BASED-SALE = ; (MPL-PL-AMT-TOTAL-SALES (2) - MPL-PL-AMT-OUTGO-SALES (2)) ; - (MPL-PL-AMT-TOTAL-RETURNS (2) - MPL-PL-AMT-OUTGO-RETURNS (2))

What it computes: Retail rate = product rate, plus adjustment where it applies
Rule in plain English: The working retail rate for each band is the cardholder's product rate. Where the account carries a rate adjustment and it is due to be applied, the adjustment is added on top.
COBOL as written: IF NOT-APPLY-RTL1-ADJ ; COMPUTE WSI-RATE-1 = CM-RI-RATE-1 ; COMPUTE WSI-RATE-2 = CM-RI-RATE-2 ; COMPUTE WSI-RATE-3 = CM-RI-RATE-3 ; ELSE ; COMPUTE WSI-RATE-1 = CM-RI-RATE-1 + CM-RI-ADJ-1 ; COMPUTE WSI-RATE-2 = CM-RI-RATE-2 + CM-RI-ADJ-2 ; COMPUTE WSI-RATE-3 = CM-RI-RATE-3 + CM-RI-ADJ-3
Notes: This is where WSI-RATE-1/2/3 used by the interest bands (INT-03..INT-06) actually come from. CPD110 calls it as CPS333-2400-SET-CI-RATE / 2100-SET-RI-RATE rather than computing rates inline.

What it computes: Cash rate = product rate, plus adjustment where it applies
Rule in plain English: The same rule on the cash side.
COBOL as written: IF NOT-APPLY-CASH1-ADJ ; COMPUTE WSI-RATE-1 = CM-CI-RATE-1 ; COMPUTE WSI-RATE-2 = CM-CI-RATE-2 ; COMPUTE WSI-RATE-3 = CM-CI-RATE-3 ; ELSE ; COMPUTE WSI-RATE-1 = CM-CI-RATE-1 + CM-CI-ADJ-1 ; COMPUTE WSI-RATE-2 = CM-CI-RATE-2 + CM-CI-ADJ-2 ; COMPUTE WSI-RATE-3 = CM-CI-RATE-3 + CM-CI-ADJ-3

Rule in plain English: Retail buckets 2 and 3 and cash bucket 2 each have their own rate set, following the same base-plus-adjustment rule.
COBOL as written: CPS333-2200-SET-RI2-RATE: COMPUTE WSI2-RATE-1 = CM-RI2-RATE-1 (+ CM-RI2-ADJ-1) ; CPS333-2300-SET-RI3-RATE: COMPUTE WSI3-RATE-1 = CM-RI3-RATE-1 (+ CM-RI3-ADJ-1) ; CPS333-2500-SET-CI2-RATE: (cash bucket 2)
Notes: Five rate sets in total, which is why an account can show five different interest figures on one statement.

What it computes: Regulatory floor and cap on every rate band
Rule in plain English: Once set, every rate band is clamped between a minimum and a maximum from the min/max table — but only when that table entry is switched on. This is the ceiling-rate control.
COBOL as written: IF TC-MINMAX-EFF-FLAG (MM-IDX) NOT = 1  GO TO CPS333-5000-EXIT ; IF WSI-RATE-1 < TC-MINMAX-MIN-RATE (MM-IDX) ; MOVE TC-MINMAX-MIN-RATE (MM-IDX) TO WSI-RATE-1 ; ELSE IF WSI-RATE-1 > TC-MINMAX-MAX-RATE (MM-IDX) ; MOVE TC-MINMAX-MAX-RATE (MM-IDX) TO WSI-RATE-1 ; (repeated for WSI-RATE, -2, -3 and the WSI2/WSI3 sets)
Notes: The clamp is applied band by band, not to a blended rate. If the effective flag is not 1 the whole check is skipped, so an un-flagged table entry silently disables the cap.

What it computes: Back-dated interest rate from the balance record
Rule in plain English: When interest is recalculated for a back-dated transaction the rate comes from the account balance process record rather than the live cardholder master.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WSI-RATE = ABP-INTR-RATE-1 + ABP-INTR-ADJ-1
Notes: Using the ABP snapshot is what makes a back-dated recalculation reproduce the rate in force at the time.

Rule in plain English: Back-dated provisional interest is accumulated into its own positive and negative buckets and mirrored to the GL.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WS-AMOUNT-GL ROUNDED = WSP-INT ; COMPUTE WSAR-TCPI-ACCRUED ROUNDED = WSAR-TCPI-ACCRUED + WSP-INT ; COMPUTE WSAR-TCPI-NEG-ACCRUED ROUNDED = WSAR-TCPI-NEG-ACCRUED + WSP-INT
Notes: These buckets are what CPD810's provisional roll-forward (REC-02) later proves.

What it computes: Effective MDR = global rate less base rate
Rule in plain English: The effective merchant discount rate is the scheme's global rate minus the base rate, computed separately for international, domestic and on-us traffic, then applied to that channel's volume.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WS-EMDR-M-INTL = QMTMPT-GLOBAL-RATES - WS-BSE-RTE ; COMPUTE WS-TEMP-MDR ROUNDED = ; WS-SUM-TMP-MC-CR-INTL * (WS-EMDR-M-INTL / 100) ; ADD WS-TEMP-MDR TO WS-TOTAL-PERCENT-MC-CR-INTL
Notes: Repeated per scheme (MasterCard, Visa, ...), per card type (credit, debit) and per domain (I international, D domestic, O on-us) — the same three-line shape each time.

Rule in plain English: The share of outgoing sales that failed to qualify for the best interchange rate.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WS-WORK-PERCENT ROUNDED = ; MMD-VI-AMT-NONQUAL-SALES (2) / MMD-VI-AMT-OUTGO-SALES (2)
Notes: Non-qualified volume is priced worse, so this ratio drives merchant repricing conversations.

What it computes: On-us volume as total less outgoing
Rule in plain English: On-us volume (both sides of the transaction belong to the bank) is total net sales minus outgoing net sales.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE CUR-AMT ROUNDED = ; (MMD-MC-AMT-TOTAL-SALES (X-MACT) - MMD-MC-AMT-TOTAL-RETURNS (X-MACT)) ; - (MMD-MC-AMT-OUTGO-SALES (X-MACT) - MMD-MC-AMT-OUTGO-RETURNS (X-MACT))
Notes: On-us carries no scheme interchange, which is why it is split out before pricing.

Rule in plain English: Outgoing volume less the non-qualified part is what earns the standard interchange rate.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE CUR-AMT ROUNDED = ; (MMD-MC-AMT-OUTGO-SALES (X-MACT) - MMD-MC-AMT-OUTGO-RETURNS (X-MACT)) ; - (MMD-MC-AMT-NONQUAL-SALES (X-MACT) - MMD-MC-AMT-NONQUAL-RETURNS (X-MACT))

What it computes: Average ticket with a divide guard
Rule in plain English: Average ticket is amount over count, but only when both are above zero, and a size error falls back to zero rather than abending.
COBOL as written: MOVE ZEROES TO WS-AVG-TKT ; IF WS-TOTAL-AMT-NET > ZERO AND WS-TOTAL-NBR-NET > ZERO ; COMPUTE WS-AVG-TKT ROUNDED = WS-TOTAL-AMT-NET / WS-TOTAL-NBR-NET ; ON SIZE ERROR MOVE ZEROES TO WS-AVG-TKT
Notes: The guard-then-ON SIZE ERROR pair is the house idiom for every division in the reporting programs.

What it computes: Tier rate shown as a percentage
Rule in plain English: A stored fractional rate is multiplied by 100 for display on the banded-rate report.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WS-TIER-RATE = WS-TBL-MISC-INTR-RATE (1) * 100

What it computes: Minor-unit conversion on merchant year-to-date statistics
Rule in plain English: Year-to-date and prior-year scheme statistics are held in minor units and divided by 100 for reporting.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WS-MC-YTD-OUS-SALES (X) ROUNDED = QMMSTAT-YTD-OUS-AMT (X) / 100 ; COMPUTE WS-MC-YTD-OUTGO-SALES (X) ROUNDED = ; (QMMSTAT-YTD-DOM-AMT (X) + QMMSTAT-YTD-ITL-AMT (X)) / 100
Notes: Note the direction: CP603160 multiplies by 0.01 (FX-03), this one divides by 100 — same conversion, two idioms.

Rule in plain English: The incoming transaction amount is divided by 100 and negated where the record represents a credit.
COBOL as written: COMPUTE WS-TEMP-TXN-AMT = WS-TEMP-TXN-AMT / 100 ; COMPUTE WS-TEMP-TXN-AMT = WS-TEMP-TXN-AMT * -1
